In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the $^{100}$, $^{132}$, and $^{116}$Sn nuclei are magic with respect to the neutron numbers 50, 82 and 66, respectively.
there exists a new neutron magic shell at Z =50, N =66 for $^{116}$Sn nucleus, and the $^{100}$ and $^{132} $Sn daughter nuclei are not magic.
there is no new magic shell at N=66 for $^{50}$Sn daughter, though there is a possibility of a new magic shell for $^{116}$Sn nucleus at N=66.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the $^{100}$-Sn and $^{112}$-Sn daughter nuclei are the most favourable ones in terms of the decay half-life for the $^{12}$-C and $^{16}$-O cluster decays, respectively, while $^{78}$-Ni is the most favourable one for $^{20}$-Ne cluster decay.

the $^{100}$ and $^{132}Sn$-daughter decays are the best possible candidates for the search of new neutron magic shells.

the $^{100}$ Sn and $^{132} Sn daughter products have a very high stability against neutron decay and hence the neutron magic numbers N=50,82, and 126 are well confirmed in the present work.
